features.definition: Extract and transform nested data using declarative specifications, deep path navigators, target-relative expressions (T), and control flow specifiers such as Coalesce, Call, Invoke, Ref, Val, and Spec.
features.name: Core Declarative Data Transformation and Path Access

features.definition: Validate and assert target data structures, route values, and perform conditional transformations using Match, Check, Switch, Regex, and boolean combinators like And, Or, and Not.
features.name: Pattern Matching and Structural Validation

features.definition: Perform deep assignment, value updates, and deep key/attribute deletion operations across complex nested target structures based on glom paths.
features.name: In-Place Target Mutation and Deletion

features.definition: Aggregate, fold, sum, count, flatten, bucket, and group iterable target data using specifiers such as Fold, Flatten, Group, and built-in accumulators (First, Avg, Max, Min, Sample).
features.name: Data Reduction, Aggregation, and Grouping

features.definition: Construct lazy iterable transformation pipelines with the Iter specifier, supporting operations like map, filter, chunked, windowed, split, unique, slice, takewhile, and dropwhile.
features.name: Lazy Streaming and Pipeline Processing

features.definition: Run glom transformations directly from the terminal against files or standard input across JSON, YAML, TOML, and Python formats using command-line arguments and flags.
features.name: Command-Line Interface

features.definition: Provides built-in tutorial data structures, sample models (Contact, Email), and in-memory persistence managers for interactive learning and demonstrations.
features.name: Interactive Tutorial and Sample Models

project_purpose: glom is a Python library for querying, transforming, validating, and restructuring nested data structures declaratively. It provides deep path-based navigation, pattern matching, stream processing, in-place mutations, and a command-line interface for manipulating complex Python objects and data formats.
